The screenplay should show consequences—an invalidated exam, a meeting with the dean, damage to trust, and a chance to rebuild through tutoring and honest work—rather than presenting concealment as clever or consequence-free. This gives the audience practical realism about detection and the character’s psychology without turning the scene into a reliable operational guide for evading exam controls.
